implications: A separate service needs explicit project-to-uploader admission; browser principal cannot be interpreted as the tenant project.

Define exact asset references and a durable consumer release outbox; repeated cross-canister checks alone are not exclusion.
Distinguish per-file, aggregate staging, lifetime and physical/billing budgets; do not copy the six-chunk fixture limit.
Provider retry/completion, namespace authority and final billing remain separate evidence gaps.

direct_upload_evaluation.recommendation: Direct browser-to-Caffeine upload with bounded manifest authorization; conditional on provider size enforcement, namespace/replay and independently obtained completion evidence. Evaluation only; runtime gate unchanged.

length_observation.result: Hash-tree construction accepts internally consistent metadata claiming one byte for a one-MiB leaf. No gateway called; server acceptance is unknown.

direct_upload_evaluation.reproduction: Verify pinned StorageClient.js SHA-256; isolate the unmodified slice from const MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_UPLOADS to before class StorageGatewayClient in Node VM with only WebCrypto, TextEncoder and Uint8Array. Hash new Uint8Array(1048576) with YHash.fromChunk; pass that one leaf to BlobHashTree.build with Content-Length: 1 and Content-Type: application/octet-stream. Record the root. No imports or gateway client executed.

metadata.contract: Canonical Content-Length equals admitted bytes; unique ASCII-token names ignoring case; no controls, line separators or surrounding whitespace in values. Raw budgets precede parsing. This does not authenticate actual byte length or provider behavior.
